items.title: February 2026 Google Discover Core Update Done Rolling Out
items.summary: Google's February 2026 Discover Core Update has completed rolling out after over three weeks, starting on February 5 and finishing on February 27. This broad update to systems surfacing articles in Discover aims to show more locally relevant content from websites based in users' countries, reduce sensational content and clickbait, and prioritize in-depth, original, and timely content from expert sites. It may impact non-US publishers targeting US audiences by decreasing their visibility there, but could enhance their content's performance in local regions over time.

items.title: How AI is changing SEO tools: Citation tracking, GEO & AI visibility
items.summary: AI is transforming SEO tools by shifting from content generation to infrastructure changes in research, auditing, tracking, and performance measurement, with a key finding that 88% of AI Mode citations do not match the organic top 10 results, emphasizing the need for broader topic coverage and off-site visibility. Modern SEO tools like Ahrefs, Moz Pro, and Semrush now incorporate AI-driven features for keyword suggestions, intent analysis, and brand visibility tracking across AI platforms, while new metrics focus on AI citation frequency and share of voice. This evolution highlights the importance of signals such as topic authority, community contributions on platforms like YouTube and Reddit, and video content for improving AI visibility in generative search responses.

items.title: Content Refresh for Local SEO + AI: What to Update Every Quarter
items.summary: This article outlines a quarterly content refresh strategy for B2C brands to maintain visibility in AI-driven search environments, emphasizing updates to Atomic Answers, schema markup, and local FAQs to align with AI extraction patterns and prevent content drift. It highlights the shift from traditional SEO to GEO, stressing proactive updates every 90 days to ensure entity clarity, freshness signals, and hyperlocal relevance for better AI citations and rankings. The approach aims to make content a trusted data source for AI agents, focusing on structured summaries and proof signals to dominate the citation economy.

items.title: Google Removes JavaScript SEO Warning, Says It's Outdated
items.summary: Google has removed its outdated JavaScript and accessibility guidance from the JavaScript SEO basics documentation, stating that the advice is no longer helpful as Google Search has been rendering JavaScript for multiple years. The removed section previously advised designing pages for users without JavaScript-capable browsers and testing with JavaScript turned off or in text-only browsers like Lynx. This update reflects Google's shift from broad cautions to specific technical advice, with improvements in assistive technologies also contributing to the guidance becoming obsolete.

items.title: Latest Google Search Documentation Updates
items.summary: Google recently updated its documentation with key SEO-relevant changes: on March 4, removed outdated JavaScript SEO accessibility info; on March 2, added preferred image best practices using schema.org and og:image for Search and Discover thumbnails. Earlier in February, guidance on increasing Discover visibility tied to the core update, and clarifications on Googlebot file size limits. These updates signal evolving standards for crawling, rendering, images, and Discover optimization.

items.title: Authors Guild Expands 'Human Authored' Certification Program
items.summary: The Authors Guild has expanded its 'Human Authored' certification program to include all U.S. authors and publishers, not just members. This initiative certifies books as entirely human-created to help distinguish them from AI-generated content amid growing concerns in the publishing industry. The move addresses ethical issues around undisclosed AI use in writing and editing.

items.title: Diversion Publishing Buys U.K. Indie Press
items.summary: Scott Waxman's Diversion Publishing Corp. has acquired U.K. independent publisher Influx Press Ltd., encompassing about 75 titles. The deal strengthens Diversion's international footprint in literary fiction and nonfiction. This acquisition reflects ongoing consolidation trends in the indie publishing sector.

items.title: Book Deals: Week of March 9, 2026
items.summary: Publishers Weekly reports major deals including Celadon Books acquiring North American rights at auction to Rose Himber Howse's Tricks of the Light in a two-book deal. Other notable contracts feature various fiction and nonfiction acquisitions across imprints. These deals showcase active buying in the current publishing market.

items.title: US Supreme Court Declines to Consider Whether AI Alone Can Create Copyrighted Works
items.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court has declined to review a case determining if works generated solely by AI without human authorship qualify for copyright protection. This leaves in place a federal appeals court ruling denying registration for an AI-created image. The decision impacts ongoing debates in publishing over AI-generated books and content ownership.

items.title: Hollywood Celebrities Flee the US as Woke Movie Industry Implodes
items.summary: Reports highlight celebrities like George Clooney, Ellen DeGeneres, and others relocating abroad, officially citing US political shifts but attributed by critics to audience rejection of woke content crippling box office performance. The industry faces ongoing woes from prioritizing ideology over storytelling. A viral story of a liberal fleeing to Canada underscores the exodus narrative.

items.title: Disney Pixar Removes 'Woke' Content After Fan Protests
items.summary: Disney has excised certain elements from an upcoming Pixar film following backlash over perceived woke messaging, particularly environmental themes. The change reflects persistent criticism of the studio's social issue integrations. This adjustment aims to address audience concerns amid broader industry shifts.

items.title: Billie Eilish Issues Response Amid Ongoing Backlash
items.summary: Billie Eilish responded defiantly to criticism following her controversial comments, weeks after her brother Finneas addressed similar issues. The backlash ties to prior statements on social topics drawing audience ire. Her stance highlights tensions between artists and public reactions.

items.title: March 2026 Pop Culture Releases Generate Buzz
items.summary: March 2026 features high-profile entertainment drops including Ryan Gosling's space adventure and Daredevil's comeback across movies, TV, and games. Fans anticipate a packed month of content from major platforms. These releases mark key moments in the pop culture calendar.

items.title: Top Entertainment Stories for March 8, 2026
items.summary: A roundup of the day's top entertainment headlines covers celebrity updates, Hollywood news, and global celeb buzz. Key stories include ongoing industry shifts and new announcements. The video format provides quick insights into recent developments.

items.title: SurveyMonkey Unveils New AI Tools Hub
items.summary: SurveyMonkey has launched a free AI-powered tools hub that enables marketers to instantly generate professional survey drafts from simple prompts in as little as 30 seconds, leveraging over 25 years of survey methodology and billions of historical responses. The hub also includes interactive calculators for metrics like NPS, CSAT, and sample size, along with 400 expert templates. This helps small businesses validate assumptions and strengthen decision-making without requiring an account.

items.title: A married founder duo’s company, 14.ai, is replacing customer support teams at startups
items.summary: 14.ai, a Y Combinator-backed startup founded by a married duo, operates as an AI-native customer support agency that replaces traditional customer support teams at startups by integrating with support systems and clearing ticket backlogs across channels. The company combines software and services to automate tasks, reduce human labor costs, and provide insights for revenue growth. This allows small startups to offload expensive support operations.

items.title: How 1,000+ customer calls shaped a breakout enterprise AI startup
items.summary: Narada, an enterprise AI startup, developed its solution for automating complex, multistep workflows across enterprise systems by conducting over 1,000 customer calls to understand pain points. This led to a practical AI product that users can interact with like a person, securing multimillion-dollar deals from early clients. It demonstrates real-world impact for growing businesses adopting AI.

items.title: Dify Raises $30 million Series Pre-A to Power Enterprise-Grade Agentic Workflows
items.summary: Dify raised $30 million in Series Pre-A funding to build and deploy production-grade AI applications and agentic workflows using a visual builder and integrations. It's adopted by enterprises for tasks like customer support automation and invoice auditing. This platform enables small to medium businesses to operationalize AI without heavy engineering.

items.title: Microsoft says ungoverned AI agents could become corporate 'double agents.' Its fix costs $99 a month.
items.summary: Microsoft launched Agent 365 and Microsoft 365 Enterprise E7 to govern and secure enterprise AI agents, addressing risks of ungoverned agents being exploited. Agent 365 provides centralized control for observability and security at $15 per user per month. This platform move helps businesses safely deploy AI agents.

items.title: Rethinking startup engineering: From heavy teams to market-ready MVPs in weeks with AI
items.summary: AI tools are enabling startups to build market-ready MVPs in weeks with smaller teams by automating coding and coordination. This reduces risks and allows focus on customer acquisition. It impacts small businesses by lowering development barriers and speeding up validation.
